claims.claim: The original Dolma dataset is an open three-trillion-token English corpus built from web content, scientific papers, code, public-domain books, social media and encyclopedic materials.
claims.notes: This describes the original Dolma dataset, not every later Dolma-family release.

claims.claim: The original Dolma Toolkit curation workflow consists of tagging documents, optional deduplication, mixing and filtering, and tokenization.
claims.locator: CLI help; Example: Process Wikipedia, steps 1–4
claims.notes: CLI behavior and command options are pinned to Dolma Toolkit v1.2.1; the dataset snapshot is a separate version dimension.

claims.claim: The Dolma document format requires id, text and source fields, with added, created and metadata fields optional.
claims.locator: Dolma Document Format; Directory Structure; attributes sidecar convention
claims.notes: This describes the v1.2.1 Toolkit document and sidecar contract; source adapters must preserve real provenance.

claims.claim: Dolma stores tagger and deduplication outputs under attributes subdirectories while preserving the source document directory structure for alignment.
claims.locator: Dolma Document Format; Directory Structure; attributes sidecar convention
claims.notes: This describes the v1.2.1 Toolkit document and sidecar contract; source adapters must preserve real provenance.

claims.claim: Dolma's documented dedupe command uses an in-memory Bloom Filter and can produce false positives; duplicate decisions are represented as attributes for later mixing.
claims.notes: Pinned to Toolkit v1.2.1; a Bloom-filter hit means possibly present, not an exact duplicate proof.

claims.claim: Dolma Mixer combines streams, merges named attributes, and supports include/exclude filters expressed with JSONPath as well as span replacement.
claims.notes: Mixer config syntax is pinned to v1.2.1; validate config against the installed CLI before large output generation.

claims.claim: The v1.2.1 tokens command writes a concatenated token array and an index CSV containing start, end, source path and document id.
claims.locator: Output format; metadata CSV columns start, end, path and id
claims.notes: These are the documented v1.2.1 output columns; later toolkit or Dolma 3 formats may differ.

claims.claim: The current allenai/dolma3 README describes Dolma 3 Mix as a 5.9T-token pretraining dataset, Dolma 3 Dolmino Mix as 100B tokens, and Dolma 3 Longmino Mix as 50B tokens.
claims.notes: Pinned to commit 1a9daced (2026-04-20). These repository descriptions are separate data products, not a single combined corpus.

claims.claim: The Dolma Toolkit repository and the Dolma 3 repository are separate software/data artifacts: the former documents the dolma CLI, while the latter publishes Dolma 3 dataset descriptions and reconstruction recipes.
claims.locator: Dolma 3 README compared with Dolma Toolkit v1.2.1 getting-started docs
claims.notes: This is a derived distinction between the recipe/data repository and the separately versioned Toolkit CLI.

claims.claim: The original Dolma dataset release uses the ODC-BY license according to the official repository and dataset card.
claims.notes: ODC-BY is the dataset-level statement; original source licenses, attribution, privacy and redistribution restrictions still apply.

claims.claim: Dolma Toolkit v1.2.1 was published on 2025-07-07.
claims.notes: This is the Python/CLI package release date, not the Dolma Dataset v1_7 snapshot date.

claims.claim: The current AI2 training-data documentation describes Dolma 3 as the current data family for OLMo 3.
claims.notes: This is a living documentation page, not a versioned Toolkit CLI reference; use a release tag for command and API claims.
